summary: Short-lived streaming connections cause adaptive-linger inflation leading to periodic p99 latency cliffs
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Narrato AI) reported periodic p95/p99 latency cliffs on streaming generation starting 2026-03-12 morning. Spikes affect short lived streaming calls (single prompt -> immediate close) used by their products for ephemeral assistant responses.

Impact:
- Intermittent p99 latency spikes up to 4s (baseline ~220ms) for streaming endpoints.
- Client-side perceived timeouts and some 504s for requests that hit top of the long-tail.
- Affects a portion of requests for this dedicated tenant (~5-8% of traffic during peak).

Environment:
- prod | us-east-1 dedicated pool for Narrato AI
- Serving runtime version: 2026.02.1
- Continuous-batcher config: adaptive-linger enabled (min_linger_ms=2, max_linger_ms=120, target_batch_tokens=2048)

Steps to reproduce (observed + synthetic):
1) On prod, observe Narrato's route during peak window (08:00-10:00 UTC) for p95/p99 graphs.
2) Synthetic repro: spawn 2000 short streaming connections (single short prompt, client closes after stream) across 250 clients with ~10 QPS each for 3 minutes.
3) Measure p95/p99 for streaming responses; watch batcher metrics (linger_ms distribution, batch_size distribution, flush_count).

Observed metrics and traces:
- Periodic ~7 minute cadence in p99 cliffs correlated with spikes in batcher_linger_samples and an uptick in 'linger_entropy' metric (internal).
- KV-cache sync latencies also show small coincident increases (~5-20ms) during cliffs.
- Traces show many small requests being buffered and then flushed together causing queueing at the head-of-line for short streams.
- No increase in GPU saturation or host-level CPU/mem during events.

Initial hypothesis:
Adaptive-linger algorithm is reacting to short-stream dominated traffic by inflating its linger window for longer than expected (linger hysteresis), which causes transient accumulation of short requests into larger flushes and results in periodic tail latency cliffs. The algorithm's state seems to drift under oscillatory traffic patterns; once linger inflates, it takes a few cycles to decay.

Investigation notes:
- Correlated Datadog dashboard: dashboards/datadog/streaming-batcher/narrato-p99-20260312 (internal link in comments).
- Flamegraphs from sampled traces show queueing time as dominant contributor to p99.
- Checked rollout history: adaptive-linger config change rolled via config-service 2026-02-28 for all dedicated pools. No code deploys coincident with first reported date.
- Reproduced locally with synthetic harness; toggling adaptive-linger off prevents cliffs.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- For Narrato's dedicated pool we set adaptive-linger.enabled=false and applied static linger_ms=8 on 2026-03-12 13:20 UTC. Immediate reduction in p99 observed within 60s during next flush cycles.
- Alert rule created to detect 'linger_ms > 50ms for >30s' on customer pools.

Follow-up / next steps:
- Engineering to add a decay cap to adaptive-linger (max_decay_ms) to limit hysteresis. (ENG-PR planned)
- Add regression test in synthetic harness simulating high-count short streams to catch oscillatory cases.
- Consider tenant-aware adaptive parameters (short-stream-heavy tenants get conservative defaults).
- Postmortem and design doc update scheduled.

Resolution notes (temporary):
- Workaround applied at 2026-03-12; customer confirmed improvement in follow-up call. We have not rolled the change cluster-wide. Will coordinate broader fix after engineering design review.
